scenarios.nativeOutcome: The native Core owns anonymous authority, durable send, and transcript convergence; every surface presents the native messenger.
The server-authorised identified owner sees the same native conversation list and transcript on every surface.
Owner A state is inaccessible before owner B authority can be used.
One durable native row survives restart and is dispatched when current authority and connectivity are restored.
Every retry keeps the original clientMessageId and duplicate acceptance converges through transcript reconciliation.
An ACCEPTED row survives interruption and becomes RECONCILED without returning to the send path.
A current-authority stream hint triggers authoritative refetch; a stale stream cannot mutate native state.
Older observations cannot undo a newer list result or a successful rendered-through acknowledgement.
Conditional refresh updates the protected last-known-good projection and offline recovery retains it.
The native messenger renders validated FAQ content locally and authorised Help Center responses directly.
Attachment chat send remains unavailable on every surface until canonical conversation binding is defined.
The native Core registers the platform token, authorises every hint before presentation, and retires owner-scoped intent at logout.
Every surface forwards the identifier to native Core and presents only after transcript authorisation succeeds.
Microphone and notification permission remain host or native-UI initiated; denial leaves text chat available.
Native and bridge diagnostics expose only structured safe fields and never content or credentials.
